clue.text: Congratulate Penny and Jack

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny
to jack something up is to lift it

explanation.surface: Someone offers congratulations to a couple called Penny and Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack looks like a name beside Penny, but it is the verb, as in jacking up a car.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone is to commend them warmly, which is what congratulating does.

clue.text: Drunk done with drinking litres before date

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the abbreviation goes inside the word for done with

blocks.note: something done with is over and past
L is the abbreviation for litres
ere is an old word for before
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: Someone has finished drinking litres of alcohol before going on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' looks like it places one piece ahead of another, but it supplies the archaic ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastered is informal British slang for very drunk, heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Get a group to perform songs on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so the phrase is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a choir is a group of singers

explanation.surface: A band manager wants to get a group to perform songs on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire something is to obtain or come into possession of it.

clue.text: Name the first woman canonised?

blocks.note: someone canonised becomes a saint, abbreviated ST
in Genesis Eve is the first woman

explanation.surface: A trivia question asking who was the first woman made a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as St Eve, the first woman made a saint sounds like a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Steve is a common given name, so an example of a name.

clue.text: Economical combining bath and tinkle

blocks.note: Bath is a spa town, and a spa is a place for bathing
giving someone a tinkle is British slang for phoning them

explanation.surface: A bathroom fitting that saves water by combining bath and lavatory functions.
explanation.walkthrough: A tinkle is British slang for a phone call, so a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sparing with money or resources is frugal and uses little, much like economical.

clue.text: Terrible lyricist ruined operettas

indicators.note: something ruined has been wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A poor songwriter spoiled a run of light operas.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is an inferior writer of verse, a dabbler with no real gift.

clue.text: Roast one horse after another’s rump

indicators.note: a rump is the hind end, so only the last letter is taken
after says the following pieces come behind the selected letter

blocks.note: final letter
I is the Roman numeral for one
a pinto is a piebald horse

explanation.surface: A cook roasts horsemeat cut from the rump, one horse after another.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to criticise them harshly, and to rip into is the same fierce attack.

clue.text: Unacceptable consequence of going for ninety-nine?

blocks.note: first meaning: an informal phrase for not allowed
second meaning, read as two words: settling for a score one short of a hundred leaves you without a century

explanation.walkthrough: A ton is a hundred, so going for 99 gives NO TON; split differently it is the phrase NOT ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not on is a British idiom meaning it is not acceptable behaviour.

clue.text: Yankee wearing crown and jeans heading for immortality on Netflix, say

indicators.note: someone wearing something has it around them, so the letter sits inside the word for crown
the heading of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: the pate is the crown of the head
Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet
Levi's are a famous brand of jeans
opening letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American in a crown and jeans seeks lasting fame through a streaming series.
explanation.definitionFit: Netflix is a subscription service, an example of television that viewers must pay for.

clue.text: Ball made square bobbles around

indicators.note: something that bobbles around moves about unsteadily, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A round ball has been pressed square and wobbles about.
explanation.definitionFit: A masquerade is a formal dance where guests wear masks, a kind of ball.

clue.text: A lot stay over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for stay is read back to front

blocks.note: to stop somewhere is to stay there

explanation.surface: Someone stays on for a long time, perhaps past a welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots, as in pots of money, is an informal way of saying a large amount.

clue.text: To wet trousers permitted during it?

definitions.text: To wet trousers permitted during it?

indicators.note: something happening during a thing sits inside it, so the word for permitted goes within the pronoun

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
to let someone do something is to permit it
when it is wet outside, it is raining

explanation.surface: A toddler asks, half hopefully, whether wetting one's trousers is allowed while learning to use the potty.
explanation.walkthrough: The word trousers does no wordplay work beyond the picture. Read whole, the clue describes the very process in which wet trousers are tolerated.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet training is teaching a small child to use the lavatory, a period when accidents with clothing are expected and forgiven.

clue.text: Uncontrolled diving off reef allowed to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent means only part of the phrase is used, so the letters lie within the run of words

blocks.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: A diver plunging off a reef is permitted only within limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off reef' tempts an anagram of reef, but the whole answer sits in o(FF REEF ALL)owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Free fall is the stage of a skydive before the parachute opens, when the body drops unchecked.

clue.text: Dreadful father turned up knackered half-way through family movie

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top, so backwards
something half-way through another sits in its middle, so the word for knackered goes inside

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
all in means exhausted
PG, parental guidance, is the film rating for family viewing

explanation.surface: A worn-out dad arrives half-way through a children's film.
explanation.walkthrough: Knackered is British slang for exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Appalling means shockingly bad or awful, which is what dreadful means.

clue.text: Company that might travel to Peru for a change

indicators.note: making a change means altering things, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A business considers relocating to Peru for a fresh start.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a group of performers, often a touring company that moves from venue to venue.

clue.text: Nasty dry peach Amy peeled is thick-skinned type

indicators.note: something nasty is spoilt, so the letters are mixed into a new order
peeling strips off the outer skin, so only the inner letter of the name stays

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
middle letter

explanation.surface: Amy peels an unpleasant dry peach, and she is not easily offended.
explanation.walkthrough: Thick-skinned type also suggests an insensitive person, and the peach has thick skin too.
explanation.definitionFit: A pachyderm is a large thick-skinned mammal such as an elephant or rhinoceros.

clue.text: Encouragement to buy rotten spud is reasonable

indicators.note: something rotten has decayed and lost its shape, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: an ad, or advertisement, urges people to buy
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A sales pitch for a rotten potato is apparently fair enough.
explanation.walkthrough: A spud is an everyday British word for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: When an argument adds up, it makes sense and holds together logically, so it is reasonable.

clue.text: Do bone work at archaeological site

blocks.note: the shin bone is the tibia
a dig is an excavation

explanation.surface: An archaeologist sets out to work on bones at an excavation.
explanation.walkthrough: Do is not a verb here but a noun for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is a British informal word for a party, and a shindig is a lively party.

clue.text: American’s outside in Washington cutting extremely lush greenery

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its two end letters, so only those are kept
in places those letters inside the abbreviation for the capital city
cutting into something means going inside it, so the group sits within the word for extremely

blocks.note: very and extremely are synonyms
Washington, D.C. is the US capital
first and last letters

explanation.surface: An American abroad takes in the lush gardens around the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the city's initials hold the end letters, and the word for extremely holds both. The 's only serves the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdancy is the quality of being verdant, meaning abundant fresh green vegetation.

clue.text: Plan maximum length of drive to put Alfa Romeo on

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece on another sits above it, so the car abbreviation comes first

blocks.note: the initials of the car maker
a vehicle's range is how far it can go

explanation.surface: Someone plans the longest possible trip in an Alfa Romeo.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange something is to organise or plan it in advance.

clue.text: That secret agency register primarily prejudices bohemian lefties

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: so can stand for that, as in 'I told you so'
the CIA is the US intelligence agency
a register is a list of names
opening letter
a bohemian lifestyle is artistic and unconventional

explanation.surface: A spy agency's list exposes the biases of left-wing bohemian types.
explanation.definitionFit: A socialist party is a political organisation on the left, so a body of lefties.

clue.text: Reveal secrets of complete eclipse

blocks.note: to out someone is to expose their secrets
to do a task is to complete it

explanation.surface: Revealing all about a total eclipse of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: Eclipse is the verb here, meaning to overshadow, not the astronomical event.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse a rival is to surpass them, which is what outdo means.

clue.text: Lady’s shoes Mike put in litter

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the letter goes within the word for litter

blocks.note: a litter is a brood of young animals such as pups
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A woman's shoes were thrown into the rubbish by a man named Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: Litter looks like rubbish, but it is a brood of young animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumps are light slip-on shoes without fastenings, commonly worn by women.

clue.text: Boss learning that deputy’s back has left

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only that is picked
something that has left is no longer there, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: study is the act of learning
final letter

explanation.surface: A boss learns that the deputy has quit.
explanation.walkthrough: Boss is not a manager here but an ornamental knob on a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised ornamental knob or projection, and a stud is a similar decorative stud on leather or wood.

clue.text: Shopkeeper Ronnie played with grommets reduced by 50 per cent?

indicators.note: playing with things moves them about, so the letters are rearranged
cutting by half means only the first half of that word survives

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
first half of the eight-letter word

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper called Ronnie fiddles with half his stock of grommets.
explanation.walkthrough: Grommets are metal eyelets, the very thing such a shop sells. An ironmonger is the British name for a hardware store owner.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironmonger is a trader who sells tools and hardware, so a particular kind of shopkeeper.

clue.text: Ancient running joke in the middle of Coriolanus taken the wrong way

indicators.note: in places the running joke inside the turned-round middle letters
the middle of a word is its central letters, so only those two are kept
the wrong way round means backwards, so those central letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: a machine that is running is on
a gag is a joke
the fifth and sixth of its ten letters

explanation.surface: A long-running joke in Shakespeare's Coriolanus is misunderstood by the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Long ago describes something from far back in the past, which is what ancient means.

clue.text: Rate cheapest EE mobile packages

indicators.note: packages means contains, so the phrase before it holds the letters inside

blocks.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: A shopper compares the cheapest phone deals from the network EE.
explanation.walkthrough: EE is a British mobile phone network.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone is to rate them highly, to value and respect them.
